Implementation complete. Here is the final report.

## Result
- Goal/task: G-20260801T041653421243Z-2d98487f / T-20260801T041653422672Z-c4815d7a
- Role: Implementer (Claude Code, headless runner)
- Status: complete (implementation + tests green; loop owns delivery)

## What changed or decided
Added a two-factor **`migration` MergeGate mode** to `scripts/mergegate_check.py` — a repository-wide mirror change delivered as a **re-run proof**: the PR's `.shiki` diff must equal the output of re-running a migration **registered on the base branch**.

- `migration_decision(pr)` — marker (`<!-- shiki:migration -->`) + `mergegate:migration` label, same message as `contract_decision` when the label is missing.
- `resolve_base_migration_registry` — reads `scripts/shiki_migrations.py` from the **base branch** via `git show origin/<baseRefName>:…` and execs it (the security property, per the scope amendment: `subprocess` inside `mergegate_check.py`, no new workflow flag, no reliance on the `.shiki`-only base snapshot for `scripts/`).
- `enforce_migration` — resolves + runs the base migration's `apply` against a copy of the base `.shiki`, then compares the diff change-set to the head byte-for-byte, with a distinct block per shape.
- Wired into `main()`: decision, mutual-exclusion with all 4 existing modes, no task/goal-id requirement, and a dispatch branch.

**Non-obvious defect I had to solve:** `github_pr_body` inlines the task's `scope` **and** `acceptance_checks` verbatim, and one acceptance criterion contains a **bare** marker mid-sentence — a substring/code-span match would have self-blocked this task's own implementation PR on the "label missing" error. I made the marker **line-anchored** (strict hardening; the loop-owned task JSON is out of locks so I couldn't reword the criterion) and added an end-to-end regression test that builds the real PR body from the stored task and asserts no self-declare/no-error.

## Checklist status
- Skill Gate: tdd (red→green), code-review (self-review pass — found & fixed the self-block + broadened fail-closed exception handling)
- TDD: `tests/test_migration_mode.py` (24 tests) drives the real gate for every mandated case incl. the self-defining-migration attack against a real git repo
- Adversarial: `scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh` — self-defining-migration attempt + one-byte deviation, both against a real git repo (exercises base-registry resolution end-to-end)

## Evidence

- `py_compile scripts/*.py` OK; `shellcheck`, `module_boundaries`, `control_plane`, `workflow_lint`, `migrations`, `malicious_pr`, `schema_drift` all pass
- Scope: only the 3 locked files changed (`mergegate_check.py`, `test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh`, new `tests/test_migration_mode.py`); the `.shiki/tasks|locks/…c4815d7a.json` changes are pre-existing loop-owned dispatch state, untouched by me
